content: 1. The combination of Brahmabuti, Centella Asiatica, and Hydrocotyle Gotu Kola is used for specific indications, with dosing regimens tailored to the condition being treated. Oral doses include 60 mg taken twice to three times daily, 600 mg taken three times daily, or 1 cup of tea made with 600 mg of dried leaves in 150 ml of water taken three times daily. Topical application involves the use of a 1% cream applied daily. 2. Indications for use include abdominal disorders, aphrodisiac purposes, common cold/flu, fatigue, memory enhancement, varicose veins, and venous insufficiency. Topical applications are used for hypertrophic scarring, psoriasis, and wound healing. The efficacy for these uses is considered possibly effective. 3. Gotu Kola has pharmacodynamic synergism with several drugs, increasing their effects. These include amobarbital, azelastine, brompheniramine, butabarbital, butalbital, carbinoxamine, chloral hydrate, chlorpheniramine, cinnarizine, clemastine, cyclizine, cyproheptadine, dexchlorpheniramine, dexmedetomidine, dimenhydrinate, diphenhydramine, doxylamine, hydroxyzine, pentobarbital, phenobarbital, primidone, promethazine, triclophos, and triprolidine. Caution and close monitoring are advised as these interactions may enhance central nervous system (CNS) depression. 4. Gotu Kola also interacts with antidiabetic agents, including acarbose, glimepiride, glipizide, glyburide, insulin (aspart, detemir, glargine, glulisine, lispro, NPH, and regular human), metformin, miglitol, nateglinide, pioglitazone, repaglinide, rosiglitazone, saxagliptin, sitagliptin, and vildagliptin. These interactions are theoretical and of minor significance, with the exact clinical relevance unknown. 5. Adverse effects associated with Gotu Kola include gastrointestinal upset, nausea, photosensitivity, and pruritus. Topical use may cause allergic contact dermatitis and burning sensations. Large doses can lead to drowsiness, hypercholesterolemia, hyperglycemia, hypertension, hypertriglyceridemia, and sedation. 6. Contraindications include concurrent use with sedative agents, diabetes mellitus, and hyperlipidemia. Use during pregnancy and lactation is not recommended. Pregnancy Category A indicates that controlled studies in pregnant women show no evidence of fetal risk, but avoidance is still advised.
